label: copy-phase z input when next output is z or w (z-z / z-w bigram recall)
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.005% of steps) that fires only in the copy phase, and only when the input token is z (fed back after being copied). Almost all mass (~88%) is on steps where the next output is z or w, i.e. recalling an original z z or z w bigram, at recall_idx >= 3. It is strongest in long sequences (L=9 carries ~70% of mass, L>=8 ~77%) and when the token before z was u, n, or a digit 1/2 (u-z is the strongest context; top activations are ...u z z / u z w). It never fires in the original or delimiter phase, on any input other than z, or on the first occurrence of a token. Precision is low: most copy-phase z->z/w steps stay silent, and adding a prev_tok in {u,n,1,2} filter raises precision to ~0.32 but halves recall, so what selects the active subset is not fully captured.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=z (+3.76), prev_tok=u (+2.91), in_tok=z (+2.74), phase=2 & out_tok=w (+2.61), out_tok=w (+2.35), phase=2 & out_tok=z (+1.72). Lower it: orig6=1 (-1.74), orig8=- (-1.48), in_count=1 (-1.32), orig7=- (-1.18).
